clue.text: One against endless search for period pieces

parts.note: an anti is a person who is against something

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for search is cut off

parts.note: a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to an unending hunt for old furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One against' reads as A plus a word, but it is a noun phrase: an anti is one who opposes. 'endless' trims QUEST to QUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiques are old collectable objects made in an earlier era, hence pieces from a past period.

clue.text: Salsa celebrated across this region of France

indicators.note: across means the answer runs across the two words that follow-on into one another

explanation.surface: Salsa dancing is celebrated throughout a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' signals letters spanning SALSA CELEBRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region in north-eastern France bordering Germany.

clue.text: Propose this without the man's medicine

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it

indicators.note: without means the letters for the man's are removed from the rest

parts.note: his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: Suggesting a medicine without the man's own remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLE + THIS = TABLETHIS; 'without' removes HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a pill, a solid dose of a drug, so it is a form of medicine.

clue.text: Question a sailor's country

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Asking a sailor which country he comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a Gulf state on a peninsula in the Persian Gulf, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Time of year seeing one of five bison, perhaps suppressed by Spain

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down beneath, so in this down clue the Spain letter sits on top

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together
a bison is an example of an ox, a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A time of year when a quintuplet bison is kept down by Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'suppressed by' puts E above QUINOX.
explanation.definitionFit: An equinox is either of the two dates each year when day and night are equal in length.

clue.text: Direction of leading attraction from the east?

parts.note: a side that is one up is leading

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the word for attraction runs backwards

parts.note: a draw is an attraction, something that draws crowds

explanation.surface: Asks which way a top attraction lies when approached from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, coming 'from the east' means reading right to left. 'leading' means one up, ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward is a direction of travel, towards a higher position.

clue.text: What posters need may be a right to wear hat

indicators.note: to wear means the hat goes around the letters, like a hat worn on a head

parts.note: a pillbox is a small round brimless hat

explanation.surface: Fly-posters may need a right to wear a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' looks like bill-stickers, but means people posting letters. A pillar box is a British red post box. 'to wear' puts AR inside PILLBOX.
explanation.definitionFit: People sending letters need a pillar box, the free-standing red British post box, to post them.

clue.text: A student fad mainly about a time in prison once

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for a student

indicators.note: about means the shortened fad word goes around the following letters
mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a craze is a fad

explanation.surface: A student's passing fad about doing a stretch in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the British L-plate. 'mainly' cuts CRAZE to CRAZ; 'about' puts AT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz is the island prison in San Francisco Bay, closed in 1963, so a former prison.

clue.text: Edward, moving up, longed for such a house

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up means the name is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
ached means longed, yearned

explanation.surface: Edward, getting on in life, longed for that kind of house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving up' turns TED into DET.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached house stands alone, not joined to another, so it is a type of house.

clue.text: Subversive type to use bar, drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the words before it are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is told to make use of the bar while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately undermines or wrecks things, the very picture of a subversive person.

clue.text: Extract energy within the law

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: Legal advice about drawing power out of something without breaking any rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' looks like an insertion signal, but 'within the law' is simply the definition of LICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or obtain a response or information, so it is a synonym of extract as a verb.

clue.text: Boo joker, losing way

indicators.note: losing means the letters for way drop out of the joker word

parts.note: a jester is a joker
ST, for street, is a way

explanation.surface: An audience boos a joker who has lost his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ST out of JESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock with shouts, as booing does, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Permission to proceed — there's headroom enough

definitions.meaning: official authorisation to go ahead, as for a plane to take off
the space left between a vehicle and a bridge or ceiling above it

explanation.surface: Air traffic control grants permission to go ahead because there's enough space overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance means both official go-ahead and the gap left beneath an overhead obstacle.

clue.text: Greek credit mainly applied to arts, oddly

indicators.note: applied to means the shortened credit word is attached after the picked letters
oddly picks the first and third letters of the word arts
mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tick is credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Describes how credit might be awarded to arts students, by odd ones only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit. 'oddly' gives AT from ARTS; 'mainly' cuts TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means relating to Attica or ancient Athens, so it is an adjective meaning Greek.

clue.text: Team sent back to capture live goat

indicators.note: to capture means the reversed team word holds the next piece inside it
sent back means the team word is read in reverse

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A team is sent home after catching a live goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns XI into IX, which then holds BE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with large curved horns.

clue.text: Pretty girl holding a gun must be game

indicators.note: holding means the girl word wraps around the next letters

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A beauty with a pistol must be game for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like an adjective meaning willing, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into scoring holes.

clue.text: One's heart a prisoner in this?

definitions.text: One's heart a prisoner in this?

parts.words: One's heart a prisoner in this?
parts.note: the bony enclosure around the chest is pictured as a cage that holds the heart captive

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lovelorn line about a captive heart.
explanation.walkthrough: A heart held prisoner suggests romance, but the cage is the literal set of bones around the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form a cage-like frame of bone enclosing and protecting the heart and lungs.

clue.text: Pretentious editor subject to influence

indicators.note: subject to means placed beneath, so in this down clue the editor goes under the influence word

parts.note: to affect is to influence

explanation.surface: A pompous editor is easily swayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to influence' reads as one phrase, but 'subject to' places ED below AFFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected behaviour is artificial and designed to impress, a synonym of pretentious.

clue.text: Party with common sense exhibiting hunger

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party
nous is British slang for common sense

explanation.surface: A sensible partygoer showing an appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British informal for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means extremely hungry, so it describes someone displaying great hunger.

clue.text: Anxious father confronting a violent thug

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of, so the father abbreviation comes first

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters of thug are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A worried dad facing down a brutal thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronting' means standing in front of, so the father abbreviation leads; 'violent' is the scrambling signal acting on the thug alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught describes a state of tension and worry, so it is a synonym of anxious.

clue.text: Cheeky young lad involved in raising cheeky theory

indicators.note: raising says the hidden letters are read backwards, upwards in this down clue
involved in means the answer is wrapped up inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheeky lad gets caught up in promoting a cheeky theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'involved' in the definition, leaving 'in' unexplained; 'involved in' is the hiding signal. 'raising' turns EKYT, from cheEKY Theory, upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is an informal word for a mischievous child, a cheeky little boy.

clue.text: Foreign Office axes cunning

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK's diplomatic ministry
x and y are the two axes of a graph

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office makes crafty cuts to its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like a verb meaning cuts, but it is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy means sly and crafty, like the proverbial fox, so it is a synonym of cunning.

clue.text: Pay for mature clip from film

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay for it
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A paying for a mature film clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film material, so a clip is a piece of footage.

clue.text: Cheerful Jamaican's first international in cricket ground

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Jamaican's
in means the international letter goes inside the ground

parts.note: the Oval is a cricket ground in south London

explanation.surface: A cheerful Jamaican plays his first international at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a Test cricket ground in London. I goes inside OVAL after J.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means good-humoured and jolly, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Could this produce a tissue, we hear?

definitions.text: Could this produce a tissue, we hear?

parts.words: Could this produce a tissue, we hear?
parts.note: the noise of the act is written atishoo, which sounds like a tissue

explanation.surface: Wonders whether something might bring out a handkerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atishoo' is the British spelling of the noise made, which sounds like 'a tissue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of this explosive nasal expulsion is written atishoo, matching 'a tissue' in pronunciation.

clue.text: Vote in the French, welcomed by European court

indicators.note: welcomed by means the French article is taken inside the other letters

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French party being voted in, welcomed by a European court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' means the French article is taken in by the other two pieces, which surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect someone is to choose them by ballot, which is exactly to vote them in.

clue.text: Cheap wicket taken by Bradman after criticism?

indicators.note: after means the Bradman piece comes after the criticism piece

parts.note: a knock is a piece of criticism

indicators.note: taken by means the wicket letter is held inside the name

parts.note: Don Bradman was the great Australian batsman
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: Bradman snaps up a wicket cheaply after taking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman is cricket's most famous batsman. 'taken by' puts W inside DON to give DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockdown price is a heavily reduced one, so knockdown is an adjective meaning cheap.

clue.text: Villain travelling north in luggage van knew

indicators.note: travelling north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in means the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crook heading north in a luggage van knew something.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the hiding signal. 'travelling north' reads EVANK, from luggagE VAN Knew, upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest, unscrupulous man, an old word for a rogue or villain.

clue.text: Seeing posh car from Yorkshire, these people cause controversy

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t', so a Yorkshireman would say t' Rolls
a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Spotting a Yorkshireman's posh motor, some people stir up a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously cuts 'the' to t'. A Rolls-Royce is the classic British luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolls are people who post provocative messages online to start arguments.

clue.text: Wild parties gatecrashed by a freeloader

indicators.note: gatecrashed by means the single letter barges into the middle of the rearranged letters
wild suggests the letters of parties are running riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Riotous parties are invaded by a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges PARTIES to PARSITE; 'gatecrashed by' inserts A.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others without giving back, a figurative synonym of freeloader.

clue.text: Cleaner shifting detritus without it?

indicators.note: shifting suggests the letters of detritus are moved about into a new order
without means the letters of the word it are left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A cleaner moving rubbish about without picking it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting ... without it' rearranges DETRITUS once I and T are taken out of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for wiping away dust, so it is a cleaning tool, a cleaner.

clue.text: Wake-up call about mask and life on the outside

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a veil masks the face

indicators.note: on the outside picks the outer letters of the word life

explanation.surface: A rousing call about masks and life outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' takes L and E from LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to rouse soldiers in the morning.
